9impl ImageColorSpace {
10    fn num_components(&self) -> u8 {
11        match self {
12            Self::Gray => 1,
13            Self::Rgb => 3,
14            Self::Cmyk => 4,
15            Self::Unknown(num) => *num,
16        }
17    }
18}
19
20pub(crate) fn decode(data: &[u8], params: &ImageDecodeParams) -> Option<FilterResult<'static>> {
21    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::stream::ImageColorSpace;
22
23    let settings = DecodeSettings {
24        // PdfCraft patch: (#3179) with no /ColorSpace in the image dictionary the colours come from
25        // the JP2 header (ISO 32000-2 §7.4.9), so its palette (`pclr`) is applied here; with a
26        // /ColorSpace the header colour data is ignored, and an /Indexed space takes the raw indices.
27        // A /ColorSpace that does not resolve also leaves `num_components` unset: the header's
28        // colours are then the only ones there are, so the palette is applied too (raw indices
29        // would be drawn as gray).
30        resolve_palette_indices: params.num_components.is_none(),
31        strict: false,
32        target_resolution: params.target_dimension,
33    };
34
35    // PdfCraft patch (21): a JP2 colour specification naming an enumerated colour space the
36    // decoder refuses (CIEJab, enum 19, in a veraPDF fixture; YCbCr, PhotoYCC, …) made the whole
37    // image fail, so the page drew blank (#3306). Then it is decoded as if it had no colour
38    // specification, as MuPDF and Poppler draw it: grey, RGB or CMYK by its component count.
39    let repaired;
40    let image = match hayro_jpeg2000::Image::new(data, &settings) {
41        Ok(image) => image,
42        Err(_) => {
43            repaired = without_refused_enumerated_colour(data)?;
44            hayro_jpeg2000::Image::new(&repaired, &settings).ok()?
45        }
46    };
47
48    let width = image.width();
49    let height = image.height();
50    // PdfCraft patch: (#3179) a resolved palette gives colours, decoded to 8 bits like every
51    // sample; the codestream's precision is that of the indices (1 bit, say), and rescaling the
52    // colours to it kept only 0 or 255 per channel (review on #3184).
53    let palette_resolved = settings.resolve_palette_indices && has_palette(data);
54    let bpc = params.bpc.unwrap_or(if palette_resolved { 8 } else { image.original_bit_depth() });
55    let cs = match image.color_space() {
56        ColorSpace::Gray => ImageColorSpace::Gray,
57        ColorSpace::RGB => ImageColorSpace::Rgb,
58        ColorSpace::CMYK => ImageColorSpace::Cmyk,
59        ColorSpace::Unknown { num_channels } => ImageColorSpace::Unknown(*num_channels),
60        ColorSpace::Icc { num_channels: num_components, .. } => match num_components {
61            1 => ImageColorSpace::Gray,
62            3 => ImageColorSpace::Rgb,
63            4 => ImageColorSpace::Cmyk,
64            _ => return None,
65        },
66    };
67    let has_alpha = image.has_alpha();
68    let bitmap = image.decode().ok()?;
69
70    let (mut data, mut alpha) = if !has_alpha {
71        (bitmap, None)
72    } else {
73        // Extract the alpha channel.
74        let total_channels = cs.num_components() + 1;
75        let mut color_channels = Vec::with_capacity((bitmap.len() / total_channels as usize) * cs.num_components() as usize);
76        let mut alpha_channel = Vec::with_capacity(bitmap.len() / total_channels as usize);
77
78        for sample in bitmap.chunks_exact(total_channels as usize) {
79            let (alpha, color) = sample.split_last()?;
80            alpha_channel.push(*alpha);
81            color_channels.extend_from_slice(color);
82        }
83
84        (color_channels, Some(alpha_channel))
85    };
86
87    // The decoded image is always 8-bit, so if necessary we have to rescale
88    // ourselves.
89    if bpc != 8 {
90        data = scale(&data, bpc, cs.num_components(), width, height)?;
91        alpha = alpha.and_then(|alpha| scale(&alpha, bpc, cs.num_components(), width, height));
92    }
93
94    Some(FilterResult {
95        data: Cow::Owned(data),
96        image_data: Some(ImageData { alpha, color_space: Some(cs), bits_per_component: bpc, width, height }),
97    })
98}

100/// PdfCraft patch: (#3179) whether JP2 file `data` has a palette box (`pclr`) in its header box
101/// (`jp2h`, ISO 15444-1 I.5.3.4). A raw codestream has none.
102fn has_palette(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
103    boxes(data)
104        .find(|&(kind, _, _)| kind == *b"jp2h")
105        .and_then(|(_, start, end)| data.get(start..end))
106        .is_some_and(|header| boxes(header).any(|(kind, _, _)| kind == *b"pclr"))
107}
108
109/// The enumerated colour spaces (`EnumCS`, ISO 15444-1 I.5.3.3 and 15444-2 M.11.7.2) the decoder
110/// handles: CMYK, CIELab, sRGB, greyscale, sYCC, e-sRGB and ROMM-RGB.
111const DECODED_ENUMERATED: [u32; 7] = [12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21];
112
113/// PdfCraft patch (21): a copy of JP2 file `data` whose colour specification boxes (`colr`, in
114/// the `jp2h` header box) that name an enumerated colour space outside [`DECODED_ENUMERATED`]
115/// name the space the decoder assumes without one instead: greyscale, sRGB or CMYK for 1, 3 or
116/// 4 components (`ihdr`). `None` when there is nothing to change or the boxes can't be read.
117pub(crate) fn without_refused_enumerated_colour(data: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
118    let header = boxes(data).find(|&(kind, _, _)| kind == *b"jp2h")?;
119    let (_, start, end) = header;
120    let inner = data.get(start..end)?;
121    let (_, ih_start, _) = boxes(inner).find(|&(kind, _, _)| kind == *b"ihdr")?;
122    // ihdr: height (4), width (4), number of components (2).
123    let components = u16::from_be_bytes(inner.get(ih_start + 8..ih_start + 10)?.try_into().ok()?);
124    let replacement: u32 = match components {
125        1 => 17,
126        3 => 16,
127        4 => 12,
128        _ => return None,
129    };
130    // Where each refused enum is, found before anything is copied: a stream the decoder refused
131    // for another reason isn't copied for nothing.
132    let mut refused = Vec::new();
133    for (kind, body, body_end) in boxes(inner) {
134        if kind != *b"colr" {
135            continue;
136        }
137        // colr: METH (1), PREC (1), APPROX (1), then EnumCS (4) when METH is 1.
138        let colr = inner.get(body..body_end)?;
139        if colr.first() != Some(&1) {
140            continue;
141        }
142        let enumerated = u32::from_be_bytes(colr.get(3..7)?.try_into().ok()?);
143        if DECODED_ENUMERATED.contains(&enumerated) {
144            continue;
145        }
146        refused.push(start.checked_add(body)?.checked_add(3)?);
147    }
148    if refused.is_empty() {
149        return None;
150    }
151    let mut out = data.to_vec();
152    for at in refused {
153        out.get_mut(at..at.checked_add(4)?)?.copy_from_slice(&replacement.to_be_bytes());
154    }
155    Some(out)
156}

158/// The boxes in `data` (ISO 15444-1 I.4): each one's type and the start and end of its contents.
159/// Stops at the first box whose length doesn't fit.
160fn boxes(data: &[u8]) -> impl Iterator<Item = ([u8; 4], usize, usize)> + '_ {
161    let mut at = 0usize;
162    core::iter::from_fn(move || {
163        let length = u32::from_be_bytes(data.get(at..at.checked_add(4)?)?.try_into().ok()?);
164        let kind: [u8; 4] = data.get(at + 4..at.checked_add(8)?)?.try_into().ok()?;
165        let (header, size) = match length {
166            // The rest of the data.
167            0 => (8, data.len().checked_sub(at)?),
168            // An 8-byte length follows the type.
169            1 => {
170                let large = u64::from_be_bytes(data.get(at + 8..at.checked_add(16)?)?.try_into().ok()?);
171                (16, usize::try_from(large).ok()?)
172            }
173            n => (8, usize::try_from(n).ok()?),
174        };
175        let end = at.checked_add(size)?;
176        if size < header || end > data.len() {
177            return None;
178        }
179        let item = (kind, at + header, end);
180        at = end;
181        Some(item)
182    })
183}

185fn scale(data: &[u8], bit_per_component: u8, num_components: u8, width: u32, height: u32) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
186    if bit_per_component == 0 || bit_per_component > 32 || num_components == 0 || width == 0 || height == 0 {
187        return None;
188    }
189
190    // PdfCraft patch: normalize all supported bit widths without an overflowing
191    // shift or floating-point endpoint rounding, including no_std builds.
192    let max_sample = u64::from(bit_mask(bit_per_component));
193
194    let bits_per_row = (width as usize).checked_mul(num_components as usize)?.checked_mul(bit_per_component as usize)?;
195    let input_len = bits_per_row.div_ceil(8).checked_mul(height as usize)?;
196    let mut input = vec![0; input_len];
197    let mut writer = BitWriter::new(&mut input, bit_per_component)?;
198    let components_per_row = (num_components as usize).checked_mul(width as usize)?;
199
200    for bytes in data.chunks_exact(components_per_row) {
201        for byte in bytes {
202            // The numerator is at most 255 * u32::MAX + 127, which fits in
203            // u64. The rounded quotient is <= max_sample, so the cast is exact.
204            let scaled = ((u64::from(*byte) * max_sample + 127) / 255) as u32;
205            writer.write(scaled)?;
206        }
207
208        writer.align();
209    }
210
211    let final_pos = writer.cur_pos();
212    input.truncate(final_pos);
213
214    Some(input)
215}

218mod tests {
219    use super::{decode, scale, without_refused_enumerated_colour};

224    #[cfg(any())]
225    fn jpx_scale_accepts_32_bit_samples() {
226        assert_eq!(scale(&[0, 255], 32, 1, 2, 1).unwrap(), [0, 0, 0, 0, 255, 255, 255, 255]);
227    }
228
229    #[cfg(any())]
230    fn jpx_scale_keeps_supported_bit_depths() {
231        for bpc in 1_u8..=32 {
232            let bytes = scale(&[0, 255], bpc, 1, 2, 1).unwrap();
233            assert_eq!(bytes.len(), (2 * usize::from(bpc)).div_ceil(8));
234            let mut reader = BitReader::new(&bytes);
235            assert_eq!(reader.read(bpc), Some(0));
236            assert_eq!(reader.read(bpc), Some(bit_mask(bpc)));
237        }
238    }
239
240    #[cfg(any())]
241    fn jpx_scale_rejects_out_of_range_bit_depths() {
242        for bpc in [0, 33, 255] {
243            assert!(scale(&[255], bpc, 1, 1, 1).is_none());
244        }
245    }
246
247    #[cfg(any())]
248    fn jpx_scale_rejects_zero_dimensions_and_components() {
249        for (components, width, height) in [(0, 1, 1), (1, 0, 1), (1, 1, 0)] {
250            assert!(scale(&[255], 32, components, width, height).is_none());
251        }
252    }
253
254    #[cfg(any())]
255    fn jpx_scale_preserves_one_eight_and_sixteen_bit_samples() {
256        let samples: Vec<u8> = (0..=255).collect();
257        for bpc in [1, 8, 16] {
258            let bytes = scale(&samples, bpc, 1, 256, 1).unwrap();
259            let mut reader = BitReader::new(&bytes);
260            for byte in &samples {
261                let expected = match bpc {
262                    1 => u32::from(*byte >= 128),
263                    8 => u32::from(*byte),
264                    16 => u32::from(*byte) * 257,
265                    _ => unreachable!(),
266                };
267                assert_eq!(reader.read(bpc), Some(expected), "{bpc}-bit sample {byte}");
268            }
269        }
270    }
271
272    /// A JP2 header (`jp2h`) holding `ihdr` for `components` and the given `colr` bodies, with
273    /// a codestream box after it.
274    fn jp2(components: u16, colrs: &[&[u8]]) -> Vec<u8> {
275        let jp2_box = |kind: &[u8], body: &[u8]| {
276            let mut b = ((8 + body.len()) as u32).to_be_bytes().to_vec();
277            b.extend_from_slice(kind);
278            b.extend_from_slice(body);
279            b
280        };
281        let mut ihdr = Vec::new();
282        ihdr.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1]);
283        ihdr.extend_from_slice(&components.to_be_bytes());
284        ihdr.extend_from_slice(&[7, 7, 0, 0]);
285        let mut header = jp2_box(b"ihdr", &ihdr);
286        for c in colrs {
287            header.extend(jp2_box(b"colr", c));
288        }
289        let mut out = jp2_box(b"ftyp", b"jp2 \0\0\0\0jp2 ");
290        out.extend(jp2_box(b"jp2h", &header));
291        out.extend(jp2_box(b"jp2c", &[0xff, 0x4f]));
292        out
293    }
294
295    fn enumerated(e: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
296        let mut c = alloc::vec![1, 0, 0];
297        c.extend_from_slice(&e.to_be_bytes());
298        c
299    }
300
301    /// The enumerated colour spaces found in the copy's `colr` boxes, in order.
302    fn enums_in(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u32> {
303        data.windows(4)
304            .enumerate()
305            .filter(|(_, w)| *w == b"colr")
306            .filter(|(i, _)| data.get(i + 4) == Some(&1))
307            .map(|(i, _)| u32::from_be_bytes(data[i + 7..i + 11].try_into().unwrap()))
308            .collect()
309    }
310
311    #[cfg(any())]
312    fn refused_enumerated_colour_spaces_become_the_component_counts_default() {
313        // CIEJab (19) and other refused spaces, by component count.
314        for (components, refused, expected) in [(3, 19, 16), (3, 22, 16), (1, 15, 17), (4, 13, 12), (3, 1, 16)] {
315            let data = jp2(components, &[&enumerated(refused)]);
316            let out = without_refused_enumerated_colour(&data).unwrap();
317            assert_eq!(enums_in(&out), [expected], "{refused} with {components} component(s)");
318            assert_eq!(out.len(), data.len(), "only the enum changes");
319        }
320        // Several colour specifications: each refused one, and only those.
321        let out = without_refused_enumerated_colour(&jp2(3, &[&enumerated(19), &enumerated(14), &enumerated(24)])).unwrap();
322        assert_eq!(enums_in(&out), [16, 14, 16]);
323        // An 8-byte box length (LBox 1) is read too.
324        let mut long = jp2(3, &[&enumerated(19)]);
325        let at = long.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"jp2h").unwrap() - 4;
326        let len = u32::from_be_bytes(long[at..at + 4].try_into().unwrap()) as u64 + 8;
327        long.splice(at..at + 4, [0, 0, 0, 1]);
328        long.splice(at + 8..at + 8, (len).to_be_bytes());
329        assert_eq!(enums_in(&without_refused_enumerated_colour(&long).unwrap()), [16]);
330    }
331
332    #[cfg(any())]
333    fn what_the_decoder_handles_or_cant_be_read_is_left_alone() {
334        for known in [12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21] {
335            assert_eq!(without_refused_enumerated_colour(&jp2(3, &[&enumerated(known)])), None, "{known}");
336        }
337        // An ICC profile (METH 2), a component count with no default, no header at all.
338        // (Its bytes where an enum would be read say 19: only METH 1 is an enum.)
339        assert_eq!(without_refused_enumerated_colour(&jp2(3, &[&[2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 19, 0, 0]])), None);
340        assert_eq!(without_refused_enumerated_colour(&jp2(2, &[&enumerated(19)])), None);
341        assert_eq!(without_refused_enumerated_colour(&[0xff, 0x4f, 0xff, 0x51]), None);
342        // Damaged lengths: none of these may panic, and none is changed.
343        let good = jp2(3, &[&enumerated(19)]);
344        for cut in 0..good.len() {
345            let _ = without_refused_enumerated_colour(&good[..cut]);
346        }
347        for bad in [0x0000_0004_u32, 0x7fff_ffff, 0xffff_ffff] {
348            let mut data = good.clone();
349            let at = data.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"colr").unwrap() - 4;
350            data[at..at + 4].copy_from_slice(&bad.to_be_bytes());
351            assert_eq!(without_refused_enumerated_colour(&data), None, "{bad:#x}");
352        }
353    }

372    /// #3179: with no `/ColorSpace` in the image dictionary, the JP2 palette gives the colours. The
373    /// raw indices (0 and 1) used to come back as a gray image, drawn as noise.
374    #[cfg(any())]
375    fn jpx_palette_is_applied_without_a_color_space() {
376        let params = ImageDecodeParams { width: 4, height: 2, ..ImageDecodeParams::default() };
377        let result = decode(PALETTE_JP2, &params).unwrap();
378        let image = result.image_data.unwrap();
379        assert!(matches!(image.color_space, Some(ImageColorSpace::Rgb)));
380        let red = [255, 0, 0];
381        let blue = [0, 0, 255];
382        let expected: Vec<u8> = [red, blue, red, blue, blue, red, blue, red].concat();
383        assert_eq!(&*result.data, &expected[..]);
384    }

386    /// With an `/Indexed` colour space in the dictionary, the PDF supplies the palette, so the raw
387    /// indices are what the image holds.
388    #[cfg(any())]
389    fn jpx_palette_indices_stay_raw_for_an_indexed_color_space() {
390        let params = ImageDecodeParams { is_indexed: true, num_components: Some(1), width: 4, height: 2, ..ImageDecodeParams::default() };
391        let result = decode(PALETTE_JP2, &params).unwrap();
392        assert_eq!(&*result.data, &[0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0][..]);

395    /// A 1x1, 1-bit codestream (one empty packet, so its sample is the midpoint 1) as a JP2 file
396    /// whose header holds `extra` boxes after `ihdr` and `colr`.
397    fn one_bit_jp2(extra: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
398        let jp2_box = |kind: &[u8], body: &[u8]| {
399            let mut b = ((8 + body.len()) as u32).to_be_bytes().to_vec();
400            b.extend_from_slice(kind);
401            b.extend_from_slice(body);
402            b
403        };
404        let mut codestream = alloc::vec![0xff, 0x4f, 0xff, 0x51, 0, 41, 0, 0];
405        for value in [1_u32, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0] {
406            codestream.extend_from_slice(&value.to_be_bytes());
407        }
408        codestream.extend_from_slice(&[0, 1, 0, 1, 1]);
409        codestream.extend_from_slice(&[0xff, 0x52, 0, 12, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 4, 4, 0, 1]);
410        codestream.extend_from_slice(&[0xff, 0x5c, 0, 4, 0x40, 0x40]);
411        codestream.extend_from_slice(&[0xff, 0x90, 0, 10, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 15, 0, 1, 0xff, 0x93, 0]);
412        codestream.extend_from_slice(&[0xff, 0xd9]);
413        let mut header = jp2_box(b"ihdr", &[0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 7, 0, 0]);
414        header.extend(jp2_box(b"colr", &[1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 16]));
415        header.extend_from_slice(extra);
416        let mut out = alloc::vec![0, 0, 0, 12, b'j', b'P', b' ', b' ', 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x87, 0x0a];
417        out.extend(jp2_box(b"ftyp", b"jp2 \0\0\0\0jp2 "));
418        out.extend(jp2_box(b"jp2h", &header));
419        out.extend(jp2_box(b"jp2c", &codestream));
420        out
421    }
422
423    /// Review on #3184: resolved palette colours are 8-bit samples whatever the indices'
424    /// precision; an image without a palette keeps its own (1 bit here).
425    #[cfg(any())]
426    fn palette_colours_are_eight_bit_and_other_samples_keep_their_precision() {
427        let params = ImageDecodeParams { width: 1, height: 1, ..ImageDecodeParams::default() };
428        let bpc = |data: &[u8]| decode(data, &params).and_then(|r| r.image_data).map(|d| d.bits_per_component);
429        let mut palette = Vec::new();
430        for (kind, body) in [(&b"pclr"[..], &[0, 2, 3, 7, 7, 7, 255, 0, 0, 64, 128, 192][..]), (b"cmap", &[0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 2])] {
431            palette.extend_from_slice(&((8 + body.len()) as u32).to_be_bytes());
432            palette.extend_from_slice(kind);
433            palette.extend_from_slice(body);
434        }
435        assert_eq!(bpc(&one_bit_jp2(&palette)), Some(8));
436        assert_eq!(bpc(&one_bit_jp2(&[])), Some(1));
437    }
438}
